notes: What the rig does with each cron a tracked Worker config declares (docs/RIG.md, Loonext in rig mode). The rig fires every cron itself through /cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled; scripts/check-rig-crons.mjs fails when a config and this file disagree, and `--ref <ref>` checks another ref's configs against it.

run: fire it on schedule. run-expect-refusal: fire it, and when the named job has the work described in `when`, it reaches an account-wide Telnyx endpoint that rig mode refuses before any request leaves (apps/api/src/environments/policy.ts). skip: never fire it. A skipped API cron silences its liveness keys, ["ops","cron:<expr>"] and each job's, so it lists them in fingerprints. Another Worker's cron (the edge's, the guard's) is always a skip, since the rig fires only the API's, and lists no fingerprint: that Worker reports nowhere the rig's relay reads, so a listed one could only hide an event the rig's own API raises (the API runs */15 too).

Refusals are listed for every code path that can reach one, not only for what today's seed exercises: a refusal that never happens costs nothing, and one that is missing is an unexplained Sentry fingerprint in R00.

A refusal's outcome says what Sentry receives. job-fails: the job lets the TelnyxApiError out, runScheduledJobs rejects with an AggregateError that holds it (under the job's own AggregateError too, since poll-registrations, poll-port-requests and grace-and-release each collect their failures, and the release's own inside grace's), the job's heartbeat is withheld, and after its grace the liveness checker raises the job's ops fingerprint. captured: the job catches it at caught_in, reports it as its own event and returns normally, so its heartbeat is recorded and no ops fingerprint follows; follow_on_events lists what the job raises next because of it.

defects: events that mean the rig's seed or a scenario's setup is wrong, with the cause. Nothing suppresses them; R00 reports them with that cause instead of as unexplained. rigd reports the first defect that matches, so no two may match one event: `message starts` reads the event's own text, which for a cron's failure is the cron's AggregateError, so it tells an exception a job captured from the same exception inside a cron's failure.

A guard refusal (a 403 from the guard rather than the app) reaches the app as a TelnyxApiError with no code, which the app treats as a real Telnyx failure. None is expected: each one the crons can provoke is a defect.

Every cron here first asks rig_database_posture(): until the rig's database reports rig mode it throws `rig cron not run: ...`. That is an infrastructure fault for R00 to report, not an expected event, so no entry suppresses it.

refusal_match.why: The app sets no fingerprint on a refusal, so Sentry groups it by exception; its message is `Telnyx 403 on <METHOD> <path> [codes rig_endpoint_refused] ...`. A job-fails refusal arrives inside the cron's AggregateError (`cron "<expr>": ...`, the last exception), usually under the job's own AggregateError: suppress that event only when every exception in it that is not an AggregateError matches a job-fails refusal listed for that cron, since anything else in it is a real failure. A captured refusal arrives as its own TelnyxApiError event, raised while that cron runs: suppress it when the message has this text and one of the refusal's paths.

crons.note: Database scans plus pushes and texts through the guard. Scheduled sends pass the outbound destination gate, which refuses a destination outside the partition with rig_destination_refused before any request leaves. S05 and S25 depend on this cron.

Webhook replay, send recovery and outbound webhooks, which rig mode delivers to the robot sink or nowhere. Calendar sync has no connection to work on (X22). The edge relays no 10DLC or porting event, so the replay never reaches a refused endpoint.

reconcile-numbers lists the account's numbers through the guard and acts only on its own billing group. A group number with no phone_numbers row is flagged once per run, or, when its customer_reference names a settled workspace with nothing provisioning, DELETEd (provisioning.ts reconcileNumbers). The seed gives every standing number an active row, ROBOT-1, ROBOT-2 and STRANGER-1 under the Robot workspace (scripts/rig/tenants.mjs), so the sweep knows all eight. The liveness checker alerts on channels a sparse rig leaves quiet; the scenarios that use each channel judge it instead.

refusals.when: an approved campaign row with a telnyx_id and no deactivated_at has an active number whose numberAssignments entry is neither added nor pending. Each run marks the number failed and the next run clears failed entries and tries again, so this is one event per such number every 15 minutes, 96 a day each: the US-number fallback's seeded registration must record every QA-W number as added, or carry no telnyx_id.

a text_enablement_orders row is pending, action-required or in-progress with fewer than 5 attempts. Each run spends one attempt per such order and raises one event for it, so an order raises at most 5.

follow_on_events.why: The fifth refused attempt marks the order failed and says so once; nothing polls a failed order.

defects.match: message starts "reconcile: Telnyx number " and contains "is unknown to phone_numbers"
defects.means: A number in the rig's group has no live phone_numbers row. The seed writes one for every standing number, so either a row was released or lost since the last seed (run rig seed), or the group holds a number that is not a standing one and no workspace bought. One warning per number per run, 96 a day each, against the relay's 100.

defects.match: TelnyxApiError "Telnyx 403 on DELETE /v2/phone_numbers/" with no [codes ...], message starts "Telnyx 403 on DELETE /v2/phone_numbers/"
defects.means: reconcile-numbers tried to reclaim a group number that has no phone_numbers row and whose customer_reference names a settled seeded workspace, and the guard refused it because it is a standing number. Only the guard's standing-number rule stood between the sweep and the number: give the number a row or clear its customer_reference.

defects.match: level warning, message starts "reconcile: reclaimed orphaned Telnyx number "
defects.means: The same reclaim got through and a number in the rig's group was deleted. If it was a standing number, the guard's standing-number rule failed: critical.

expected_events.why: The rig texts a few times a day, so most hours have no outbound text while the 7-day baseline is not empty. S20 judges outbound texts.
The same gap for inbound texts. S21 judges them.
The rig sends email rarely. S34 judges it.
A day with no paid call lane (room, budget or a halt) leaves call events quiet. The call scenarios judge them.

crons.note: Usage goes to the Stripe sandbox, which S01's meter check reads. The inbound canary stays off because the rig sets no CANARY_* numbers. sweep-stale-calls hangs up a runaway leg through the guard's leg-command class. ring-success-watch reads api_ring_success from the rig's own database and alerts ["ops","ring-success-<platform>"] only on a drop, which takes 30 ring pushes in the 24-hour window and 30 in the week before it. On the rig that means the rig's own phones stopped ringing, so nothing suppresses it.
Email only, through the guard's Resend path; it calls no 10DLC endpoint.
Calls the public Nominatim service, which has no seam and is not on the rig's DNS block list. It only ever sees seeded synthetic addresses, once each, at one request a second, and caches the answer.
As the contact geocoder: public Nominatim, seeded synthetic addresses only.
Database read plus one warning email per crew per day; S26 judges its 80% alert.

No job but the registration poller makes a Telnyx request. telnyx-wiring-watch reads production's Telnyx wiring in production only: productionWatchRefusal stops it in rig mode before any request, so it logs that it was skipped and returns, and its heartbeat is recorded.

refusals.when: a brand or campaign row with a telnyx_id and no deactivated_at is submitted, pending, approved or suspended (each is polled), or an approved brand's campaign is a draft or deactivated (it is submitted). An approved campaign is also read a second time, for its content migration.
as retry-campaign-assignments on the */15 cron, which this job also runs once a day

crons.note: The portability check and the document upload are reached only from the porting routes, never from this job.

refusals.when: a port_requests row with a Telnyx order id is not ported or cancelled, or is voice-ported with messaging still pending: the poll's read of the order is refused

a draft port_requests row is due a resume, with no order yet (the saga creates one) or with an order and both documents (it is confirmed). The refusal is written to the row's rejection_reason and raised as its own event, once per such row per day.

crons.note: S29 fires this after backdating a workspace's cancellation. The release deletes every number that workspace holds (provisioning.ts releaseCompanyNumbers), so S29's workspace must hold no standing number: QA-C as RIG.md 3.3 lists it holds DEV-C1. See defects.

refusals.when: a workspace past its grace period still has an active 10DLC campaign to deactivate, or holds a hosted (text-enabled) number whose enablement order is not cancelled: releasing it deletes the hosted number, or the order while it is not completed

defects.match: TelnyxApiError "Telnyx 403 on DELETE /v2/phone_numbers/" with no [codes ...], inside the cron's AggregateError, contains "0 14 * * *"
defects.means: The grace job tried to release a standing number and the guard refused it: S29 backdated a workspace that holds one. The job fails before it deactivates the workspace's campaign, and S29 cannot pass. Only the guard's standing-number rule kept the number. S29 needs a workspace whose only number is one bought for the run.

crons.note: Re-mirrors subscriptions from the Stripe sandbox.

Reads /v2/messaging_optouts filtered by each workspace's own messaging profile, which the guard's read class allows. It keeps going past a workspace whose list cannot be read, reporting each one as its own Sentry message.
Retention and purge against the local database and storage; the notices are email through the guard.
Proves the Durable Object can still reach Sentry, here the loonext-rig project through the relay. Four debug events a day of the relay's 100.

expected_events.why: The canary's arrival is its assertion (#375); it is never a failure.

crons.note: Weekly founder digest. On the rig it can only describe seeded tenants, and it reaches no inbox outside the guard's Resend allowlist.
The free probes: local auth health and the webhook ledger. Nothing is billed.

Monthly recap email to every active seeded workspace. The guard sends only to Resend's test addresses, and every member the seed creates has one (memberEmail in scripts/rig/tenants.mjs, pinned by tools/rig/test/seed.test.mjs).

crons.reason: loonext-rig-edge runs on Cloudflare, never on the rig box: its mail self-test, uplink tick and dead-man fire there on Cloudflare's clock, so the rig has nothing to fire. The dead-man reports to the synthetic project as ["synthetic-infra", <component>] and to production as ["ops","synthetic-dark"], never through the rig's relay, and no liveness key watches this cron.

The guard's weekly Telnyx key inventory, a Cloudflare cron on loonext-telnyx-guard that the rig box never fires. It reports to production's Sentry as ["ops","telnyx-key-inventory"], never through the rig's relay, and no liveness key watches this cron.

The guard's hourly upkeep on Cloudflare (expired legs, the robot mailbox's arrival deadline, the first order's read-back, the balance sample and the monthly cap), which the rig box never fires. What it raises goes to production's Sentry under the guard's own keys (telnyx-guard-order-group, telnyx-balance-low, telnyx-guard-detach), never through the rig's relay, and no liveness key watches this cron.
